safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a 3-4 month history of sore and cracked skin on the hands, mainly on the palms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes sore/cracked hands/fingers for 3-4 months but does not specify that it is mainly on the palms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that symptoms are mainly on the palms reduces anatomic specificity, which can affect diagnostic clarity (e.g., palmar irritant/contact dermatitis vs other hand dermatoses) and the precision of counseling about exposures. This is unlikely to cause direct harm but may lead to less targeted management or follow-up questioning.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states NKDA, but Generated contains no allergy/adverse reaction statement.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document NKDA leaves allergy status ambiguous, which can increase the risk of prescribing or dispensing without an explicit allergy check and can also cause delays or redundant verification. Because allergy documentation is a core medication-safety element, this carries meaningful potential safety impact even when the true status is NKDA.

safety_verdicts.content: Prescribed a steroid cream to be used twice daily (BD).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes steroid cream but does not specify twice-daily (BD) use.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not specifying twice-daily use for the prescribed topical steroid can result in incorrect use (too frequent leading to local adverse effects like skin atrophy, or too infrequent leading to poor symptom control). This typically causes limited harm and is often correctable with clarification or pharmacy labeling, but may impair treatment effectiveness.
